humanEffects.notes: One of the most studied natural memory compounds. Meta-analysis of 20 studies confirms significant effect.
Mechanism is pharmacologically established — one of the most potent natural acetylcholinesterase inhibitors known.
Student populations show faster acquisition of new information in RCTs.
The basis for pharmaceutical development of cholinesterase inhibitor drugs. Effects in clinical populations are significant.

studies.title: Huperzine A for Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
studies.dose: not pooled in abstract; heterogeneous across 20 included RCTs
studies.outcome: MMSE, Hasegawa Dementia Scale, Wechsler Memory Scale, ADL, CDR
studies.result: Significant beneficial effect on cognitive function and activities of daily living vs. placebo across multiple timepoints. Methodological quality of most included trials rated high risk of bias; authors explicitly urge caution in interpretation. No trial reported severe adverse events.

studies.title: Huperzine A for Alzheimer's disease
studies.outcome: MMSE, ADAS-Cog, CDR, CIBIC-plus, ADAS-non-Cog, ADL
studies.result: Beneficial effects on general cognitive function, global clinical status, behavioral disturbance, and functional performance vs. placebo; no significant benefit on Hasegawa Dementia Scale or Wechsler Memory Scale. Adverse events mild, not significantly different from control. Authors conclude: 'only one study was of adequate quality and size... inadequate evidence to make any recommendation about its use.'

studies.title: Huperzine A for mild cognitive impairment
studies.outcome: cognitive efficacy and safety in MCI
studies.result: No eligible randomized placebo-controlled trials of huperzine A in MCI were identified; no meta-analysis could be performed. Evidence deemed insufficient to assess huperzine A's potential in MCI.

studies.title: Huperzine-A capsules enhance memory and learning performance in 34 pairs of matched adolescent students
studies.population: healthy adolescent students (junior middle school) reporting memory inadequacy
studies.result: Huperzine group MQ (115±6) significantly higher than placebo (104±9, p<0.01); language-lesson scores also markedly elevated.

studies.title: Efficacy of tablet huperzine-A on memory, cognition, and behavior in Alzheimer's disease
studies.design: RCT, multicenter, prospective, double-blind, parallel, placebo-controlled
studies.outcome: Wechsler memory scale, Hasegawa dementia scale, MMSE, ADL, safety labs/ECG
studies.result: 58% (29/50) of huperzine-treated patients improved on memory, cognitive, and behavioral function vs. 36% (19/53) on placebo (p<0.05 vs. placebo). No severe side effects reported.

studies.title: Huperzine A for the treatment of cognitive, mood, and functional deficits after moderate and severe TBI (HUP-TBI): results of a Phase II randomized controlled pilot study
studies.design: RCT, Phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot
studies.population: moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), subacute-to-chronic phase
studies.outcome: California Verbal Learning Test-II (memory/learning), Beck Depression Index
studies.result: No difference between huperzine A and placebo in memory performance at 12 weeks; the placebo group showed significant learning/memory improvement. Both groups improved on depression. Authors attribute the result to a placebo effect and caution that future TBI trials must account for it.

verdicts.claim: Memory Recall — strong evidence, moderate magnitude, 15 studies, 'meta-analysis of 20 studies confirms significant effect'
verdicts.reason: The direction is consistently positive in AD patients and one healthy-adolescent RCT, and the 20-study meta-analysis (PMID 24086396) does confirm a significant pooled effect — but that same meta-analysis and the Cochrane review (PMID 18425924) both explicitly flag high risk of bias / inadequate evidence quality, and the Cochrane MCI-specific review (PMID 23235666) found zero eligible RCTs for MCI. A modern TBI RCT (PMID 31638455) found no benefit, with placebo outperforming. 'Strong' evidence strength does not reflect the poor-quality caveat attached to every meta-analysis, and the claim doesn't distinguish AD-patient results from the thin healthy-adult evidence base.

verdicts.claim: Acetylcholine Preservation — strong evidence, large magnitude, 12 studies (mechanistic)
verdicts.reason: This is a pharmacological mechanism claim (reversible AChE inhibition) rather than a clinical-outcome claim, and it is consistently and uncontroversially described as such across every source retrieved, including the rat pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic study confirming elevated cerebral acetylcholine following huperzine A dosing.

verdicts.claim: Learning Speed — moderate evidence, moderate magnitude, 8 studies, 'student populations show faster acquisition'
verdicts.reason: Only one matching study was located: Sun et al. 1999 (PMID 10678121), a small (n=68) matched-pair RCT in adolescent students, which did show a genuine, statistically significant learning benefit. That supports the direction of the claim, but 'moderate, 8 studies' substantially overstates the size of the evidence base — this search found a single student-population RCT, not eight.

verdicts.claim: Alzheimer's Symptom Reduction — strong evidence, moderate magnitude, 10 studies
verdicts.reason: Both the Xu 1995 RCT (PMID 8701750) and the pooled meta-analyses (PMID 24086396, 18425924) show a consistent positive direction, but both Cochrane reviews explicitly conclude the evidence is inadequate for a firm clinical recommendation due to poor trial quality (mostly small, single-country studies). Characterizing this as 'strong' with unqualified 'significant effects' omits the quality caveat both Cochrane authors attach.

doseAssessment.suggestedText: 50–200mcg/day brackets the doses actually used in the retrieved trials (100–200mcg/day); the 50mcg lower bound itself was not separately tested in the trials found here.

safetySignals.signal: Our copy states huperzine A 'must be cycled 5 days on / 2 days off' to avoid cholinergic accumulation/overload, and lists GI discomfort and overdose risk with other cholinergics. The retrieved clinical trial evidence is actually milder than this framing: the 2008 Cochrane review reports 'the adverse events of Huperzine A were mild and there were no significant differences of adverse events between Huperzine A groups and control groups,' and no retrieved human trial reported severe adverse events. No human trial in this search specifically tested or validated a 5-on/2-off cycling protocol — a rat pharmacokinetic study (PMID 41781122) confirms a short plasma half-life with enhanced brain exposure on repeated dosing, which is consistent with (but does not directly prove) an accumulation rationale for cycling.

gaps: No human trial was found that specifically tests or validates the '5 days on / 2 days off' cycling protocol our copy prescribes.
The 30–60 minute acute onset claim has no supporting human trial in this search — all retrieved human RCTs measured outcomes after weeks of chronic dosing, not acute single-dose administration.
No regulatory-status information (e.g., prescription-drug classification in specific markets) was found in any retrieved abstract; this could not be verified and is not asserted.
The claimed '15 studies' (Memory Recall) and '8 studies' (Learning Speed) study counts could not be independently confirmed at that granularity from the sources retrieved in this search.
